title: Slimline econ compiler and quant probe CLI
author: Lydia Park
release_notes: Adds a lightweight econ compiler that emits tenant-default batching/caching suggestions and a small CLI to probe quantization telemetry. Non-breaking, opt-in. Suggested release notes: "Introduce Slimline Econ Compiler: generates safe defaults for batching, cache presets, and quantization hints. Includes `rwc econ probe` CLI for dry-run profiling."
description:
Motivation: many customers ask for safer, lower-risk defaults for batching and quantization that reduce unit cost without requiring heavy manual tuning. This PR introduces a compact "Slimline Econ Compiler" and an accompanying CLI (rwc econ probe) that synthesizes tenant-safe defaults (batch shapes, cache TTL estimates, and quantization hint profiles) from a short synthetic workload sample and lightweight telemetry. The goal is to provide an opt-in, reproducible path for customers to obtain conservative economics defaults and to make it straightforward for platform teams to audit and export suggestions.

What this changes (high-level): - A small compiler component (pkg/econ/compiler) that consumes workload summaries and outputs default profiles encoded as YAML-compatible presets. The compiler is intentionally conservative: it biases toward latency SLO preservation and safe cache sizing. - A CLI shim (cmd/rwc/econ_probe) that runs inside a dry-run sandbox, probes model snapshots and token-length distributions, and emits candidate defaults + a short explanation. The CLI can export to the console, to a tenant-presets bucket, or to stdout in JSON/YAML. - Telemetry hooks (agent/telemetry/econ_probe) to publish summarized quantization artifact signals (per-model bitwidth suggestions, fallback risk score) to the telemetry pipeline for later aggregation. - Unit-econ preview: a cost estimator that maps the suggested defaults to an estimated per-1M-token delta (savings or cost) with confidence bands. This is conservative and intended for decision support.

Compatibility and safety: - All defaults are opt-in and stored under a new presets namespace (presets/econ/slimline). - The compiler refuses to recommend lower-than-tested quant bitwidths for models marked as high-loss-risk in the model registry. - CLI includes a --dryrun flag and a --rollback token to ensure non-destructive operation in production accounts.

Testing and validation: - Added integration tests that run the compiler against three synthetic workload profiles and assert fallback policies preserve 95th-percentile latency under simulated load. - Added unit tests for the cost estimator and quant suggestion heuristics. - Added a small e2e smoke harness in examples/econ_probe/ that demonstrates export-to-bucket and import back into the presets loader.

Operational notes: - Telemetry events are low-volume by design (single aggregated event per probe run). - The CLI requires the existing telemetry write role and the presets write permission if export-to-bucket is used. - Suggested rollout: enable in internal Canary tenants for two weeks, collect metrics for cost delta and latency impact, then consider a staged enable for Premium accounts.

Context and related: linked to ENG-4521 (econ defaults initiative) and ENG-4670 (quant-safety signals). Related PRs: a future follow-up will add UI integration in Console to preview suggested presets before applying them.

review_thread:
Ravi Singh: Can the compiler guarantee not to recommend a quantization that increases expected loss?
Lydia Park: We added a hard guard: models with a 'high_loss_risk' flag in the registry are never proposed below 8-bit; the estimator also emits a risk_score and refuses suggestions when score > 0.2.
Camila Ortega: The telemetry schema looks fine; please include a version bump note for downstream parsers.
Lydia Park: Added econ_probe_v1.json and included schema docs in telemetry/README.
Noah Kim: CI failed on initial run due to missing mocking of registry calls. Can we add a test that covers model-flag paths?
Lydia Park: Fixed in commit d4f8a10, added registry test mocks and an integration test that exercises both permissive and guarded model states.
Ravi Singh: Approval pending an e2e run against Canary.
Ops (comment): Ran a dry run in Canary (tenant: canary-econ-01) and saw ~7% cost reduction on a synthetic webchat trace with no regression in P95 latency over 48 hours.
Ravi Singh: Approved. Camila Ortega: Approved. Noah Kim: Approved.
ci_summary: Initial CI: fail (missing mock). Second CI: pass. Checks: go-lint: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-smoke: pass, telemetry-schema-check: pass, e2e-canary-dryrun: manual passed
merge_result: Merged via squash (squash-merge). Commit message: "Slimline econ compiler + econ_probe CLI: opt-in compact defaults generator and telemetry probe". Release milestone: 2025.3. Notes: No DB migrations required; presets loader supports backward-compatible format.
notes_for_support: If customers report unexpected latency regressions after applying presets, advise them to: 1) re-run rwc econ probe --dryrun and capture the suggested defaults; 2) compare with existing batching/caching config; 3) escalate with /support including the probe output and telemetry event id. The CLI prints an event_id on success.
upgrade_guide: None required for existing deployments. To opt-in: run 'rwc econ probe --tenant <id> --export-bucket <bucket>' and then 'rwc presets apply --preset-id <id>'. The CLI prints suggested conservative TTLs and batch shapes. Admins should run the canary flow first.
